questions.question: A brute-force verifier must check every assignment for a formula containing 12 distinct propositional variables. How many rows must its truth table enumerate?
questions.explanation: Each variable doubles the rows: 2¹² = 4096 — the exponential growth that makes truth-table checking infeasible for many variables.

questions.question: To minimize a 4-variable formula, a designer draws a 4×4 grid whose neighboring cells differ in exactly one variable and circles adjacent groups of 1-cells to extract a minimal sum of products. Which tool is being used?
questions.explanation: A Karnaugh map arranges truth-table cells so adjacent cells differ in one variable, letting groups of 1-cells be merged into minimal product terms.

questions.question: Inspecting all 8 rows of a joint truth table, a student finds that whenever p→q and q→r are both true, p→r is also true — no exception row exists. The premises stand in which relation to the conclusion?
questions.explanation: Semantic entailment (⊨) holds exactly when every assignment making all premises true also makes the conclusion true — verified row by row here.

questions.question: The truth-table column for (p∧¬q)∨r is True in some rows (e.g., p=True, q=False, r=False) and False in others. Which property — true under at least one assignment — does the formula have?
questions.explanation: A formula is satisfiable when at least one row of its truth table is true; (p∧¬q)∨r has satisfying rows but is not a tautology.

questions.question: Every one of the 8 rows in the table for p∨¬p∨(q→r) evaluates to True. Classify the formula.
questions.explanation: p∨¬p is true in every row, and disjoining with (q→r) cannot change that — the formula is valid, a tautology.

questions.question: To test whether the premise set {p→q, ¬q, p} can be satisfied simultaneously, a student scans a joint truth table for a row where all three are true. How many such rows exist?
questions.explanation: ¬q forces q=False and p forces p=True, which makes p→q false; so no row satisfies all three — the set is inconsistent.

questions.question: In the formula ((p→q)∧r)∨¬s, which connective is evaluated last — the principal (main) operator that determines the formula's overall type?
questions.explanation: The formula parses as ((p→q)∧r) ∨ (¬s), so the outermost connective — the principal operator — is ∨ (disjunction).

questions.question: Evaluating (p∧q)∨r row by row, an evaluator skips computing the right disjunct whenever the left side is already true, and skips q whenever p is false. Which evaluation optimization is this?
questions.explanation: Short-circuit evaluation stops as soon as the outcome is fixed: p∧q needs no q when p is false, and x∨y needs no y when x is true.

questions.question: A gate library contains only the ↑ operator. By showing ¬p ≡ p↑p and building AND and OR from there, an engineer proves all 16 two-variable truth functions are realizable. Which property of {↑} does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: A set is functionally complete when it can express every truth function; NAND alone achieves this via ¬p ≡ p↑p and p∧q ≡ (p↑q)↑(p↑q).

questions.question: A checker builds one truth table for φ = p→q and ψ = ¬q→¬p and finds the two formulas' columns identical in all four rows. What does this column match establish?
questions.explanation: Identical truth-table columns mean the formulas share every truth value — the definition of logical equivalence (here, contraposition).

questions.question: In a 3-variable truth table, in how many rows is (p∧q)→r false?
questions.explanation: It fails only when p=True, q=True, r=False — a single row.

questions.question: In a 3-variable truth table, in how many rows is (p∨q)→r false?
questions.explanation: It fails when r=False and p∨q=True: three of the four r=False rows qualify.

questions.question: The assignment p=True, q=False, r=True makes (p→q)∨r evaluate to True. What is such a truth-value assignment that satisfies a formula called?
questions.explanation: A model is an assignment under which the formula is true — here p→q is false, but r=True makes the disjunction true.

questions.question: Scanning all 8 rows of the table for (p∧¬p)∨(q∧¬q∧r), a student finds the formula is True in none of them. Classify the formula.
questions.explanation: Each disjunct contains a conjunct of the form x∧¬x, which is false in every row; a formula with no satisfying row is unsatisfiable (a contradiction).

questions.question: After verifying every row, a logician writes 'p→q, q→r ___ p→r' to record that the conclusion is true in every row where the premises are. Which symbol fills the blank?
questions.explanation: The double turnstile ⊨ records semantic entailment — the conclusion is true in every model of the premises.

questions.question: In the 8-row table for ((p→q)∧(q→r))→(p→r), how many rows evaluate to False?
questions.explanation: The formula encodes transitivity of implication (hypothetical syllogism) — a tautology, so no row is false.

questions.question: Treating ⊕ as XOR, in how many of the 8 rows is p⊕q⊕r true?
questions.explanation: Chained XOR computes odd parity: the rows with exactly one true input (3 rows) plus the all-true row (1 row) give 4.

questions.question: In an 8-row table over p, q, r, in how many rows is p→(q→r) false?
questions.explanation: The outer implication fails only when p is true and q→r is false — the single row p=T, q=T, r=F.

questions.question: In the 4-row table for (p∧q)↔(p∨q), in how many rows is the formula true?
questions.explanation: Conjunction and disjunction agree only on the uniform rows: T↔T and F↔F hold; the two mixed rows fail.

questions.question: A 3-variable formula's truth-table column shows True in exactly 3 of the 8 rows. Classify the formula.
questions.explanation: True in some rows and false in others — neither tautology (all true) nor contradiction (all false).
